hints: A sequence tree can isolate a range by position.
Store each subtree sum and a lazy flag for reversing its sequence.
Split out the range, reverse it or read its sum, then merge it back.
analogy: A box of numbers records its total even if its contents are turned around.
example: For [1,2,3], reversing positions 1 through 2 gives [2,1,3]; the sum of positions 2 through 3 is 4.
algorithm: Use an implicit treap storing subtree size, sum, and a lazy reversal flag. Split before a and after b. For a reversal toggle the middle flag; for a query read the middle sum. Merge all pieces back, pushing flags before descent and updating metadata after structural changes. Use wide sums.
correctness: The split isolates exactly the range, and reversing a sequence does not change its sum. Correct subtree metadata and lazy propagation therefore give the requested sum and preserve all updates.
complexity: For n elements and m operations, expected O(n+m log n) time and O(n) space with linear-time construction.
